title: Performance profile custody and reflexive refresh playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: As model churn accelerates and more customers rely on Redwood-verified performance claims, we need an explicit operating model for who 'owns' a performance profile artifact, how it is signed/pinned, and a reflexive (signal-driven) refresh process that keeps published profiles accurate without manual refresh cycles.

Goal: Ship an operational playbook and automation that covers profile origination, custody transfer, automated drift detection, refresh triggers, verification gating, and signed publish/rollback. The playbook should reduce stale profile incidents to zero across verified models, cut manual republishing time by >80%, and ensure customers can rely on pinned version SLAs.

Scope: This ticket covers the product-level playbook (policy + acceptance criteria), the minimal automation hooks required to trigger a refresh flow (telemetry contracts + sampling), and acceptance criteria that RBAC-enabled signoffs and canary publish are enforced. Engineering tickets will follow to implement automation. Non-goals: full implementation of drift remediation heuristics and UI surface for profile editing (tracked separately).

Key concepts introduced: 
- Profile custody: explicit owner field in manifest (team / steward), signing identity, and retention window.
- Reflexive refresh: automatic creation of a 'refresh candidate' when operational signals diverge beyond thresholds (latency P95 drift, throughput degradation, or cost delta).
- Signed publish: profiles are cryptographically signed (or ledger-attested) at publish time with signer identity and hash in the manifest.

Success metrics: 
- Time-to-publish for a refresh candidate reduced from median 3 days -> <12 hours.
- Staleness incidents (profile claim exceeding 15% error vs observed metrics) reduced by 100% for models onboarded after implementation.
- Canary pass rate for refresh candidates >= 95% before promoted to signed publish.
- Clear owner assigned for 100% of published profiles.

Operational policy summary: 
1) Origination: When a model is onboarded, the onboarding engineer or runtime owner must create an initial performance profile draft with sample workloads, verifier sentences, cost estimates, and an owner.
2) Custody transfer: Team that operates the runtime and tests signs off using an approval workflow; custody metadata includes owner, support contact, and retention policy.
3) Publish gating: Profiles only promoted to "Redwood-verified" after passing: synthetic regression suite, shadow sampling on production for 24h, and cost sanity checks.
4) Reflexive refresh triggers: 
   - Latency drift: P95 increases > 12% relative to profile baseline over a 6-hour rolling window.
   - Throughput regression: end-to-end throughput drop > 15% for same batch configuration.
   - Cost delta: cost per 1M tokens increases or decreases by > 10% caused by infra/compiler changes.
5) Refresh candidate lifecycle: Candidate generated -> automatically runs verification suites -> canary publish (1% traffic) -> collection of telemetry for 24h -> pass/fail gate -> auto-sign or rollback.
6) Rollback and retraction: If a signed profile causes regressions for customers, we support signed rollback with a signed retraction artifact and an incident record linking to the causal change.

Telemetry contract (minimum): 
- Required metrics: p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tokens_per_second, avg_cost_per_token, error_rate, cpu_gpu_utilization.
- Must support sampling by route/model/version and provide histograms for percentiles.

Automation deliverables for phase 1 (product scope): 
- A documented playbook (this artifact).
- A small webhook contract spec that engineering uses to accept "refresh candidates" and kick off verification runs.
- A signed-manifest template with owner, signer, signature, baseline hashes, and canary-window metadata.
- Clear acceptance criteria used by SRE/Runtime team to gate automation rollout.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria below for discrete checks required to mark ticket Done.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Playbook doc (this ticket) reviewed and approved by runtime eng, QA, and security
A2: Manifest template committed to the verified-profile repo and reviewed (link in links)
A3: Webhook contract for refresh candidates defined with schema and example payloads
A4: Reflexive-trigger thresholds defined and instrumented in the telemetry spec
A5: Example refresh run documented end-to-end with a sample canary result and rollback path
A6: Ownership fields required on profile publish UI/CLI enforced (owner, contact, retention)
